title: Aurora pilot safety checkpoint & decision framework
summary: Weekly POC checkpoint to review pilot results, confirm canary thresholds and rollback criteria, finalize cutover runbook rehearsal date, and assign ownership for smoke tests and SLO alerts. Customer raised a data residency question and requested SOC2 artifacts. Agreed next step: run controlled canary (10% traffic) next Tuesday, Redwood to send security pack and a templated runbook by Friday.

SE to run extended latency/throughput run overnight and share results

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 16:00 UTC (09:00 PT)
Duration: 0:57:00
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (CSM), Priya Kapoor (Aurora PM), Diego Alvarez (Aurora SRE), Nora Ibrahim (Aurora DS), Samir Mehta (Aurora Security), Elena Brooks (Aurora VP Eng)

Summary (auto): quick recap of week, go/no-go criteria refinement, canary split plan, who runs smoke tests, ask for security documents.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll try to keep this to an hour, quick round robin?
[00:06] Priya: hey thanks, Priya here, I'll steer the outcome decisions today, Elena stepping in later.
[00:12] Diego: Diego, SRE, mostly here for the cutover and monitoring bits.
[00:15] Nora: Nora, data and evals, I have the quality numbers to share.
[00:20] Maya: perfect, Liam will go over perf, I have runbook and next steps.

--- Pilot results review ---
[00:35] Liam: ok real quick, we ran the 4-hour centerline test across the dedicated pool. median p95 latency is 210 ms for text-gen short prompts, p99 drifted to 420 ms during garbage collection windows, but average throughput sustained at about 220 rps.
[00:56] Nora: right, on quality we sampled 5000 requests, rouge and human eval benchmarks show model variant B has parity with baseline for our clinical summarization task, small hallucination rate, about 1.8% on critical entities.
[01:18] Priya: is that acceptable? the product folks say anything over 1% on named entities is risky for compliance.
[01:25] Nora: yeah, so there's a tuning knob we tried - de-dup/stop-token tuning - it reduced hallucinations but increased truncation cases, trade off.
[01:40] Liam: also the KV cache behavior helped with latencies on repeated prefixes, although in some longer contexts it falls back and you see a spike. we can configure longer cache windows but that increases memory footprint.
[01:55] Diego: memory footprint - do we have hard numbers? our infra budget for this cluster is capped.
[02:01] Liam: with 8G kv cache it added roughly 7% GPU mem, with quantized weights it's still within dedicated profile but headroom is tight if we raise sequence lengths.

--- Canary and cutover plan discussion ---
[02:25] Maya: ok proposition: start with a controlled canary next Tuesday, 10% traffic for 6 hours, monitor p95, error rate, and hallucination regression on a sampled eval set. if all gates pass we'll move to 50% for 2 hours then full cutover. thoughts?
[02:45] Elena: that's sensible, but we need explicit rollback thresholds. what exactly triggers rollback?
[02:52] Liam: propose these gates: p95 latency increases >30% from baseline for >5 minutes -> rollback. error rate >1% absolute increase -> rollback. hallucination critical entity errors >2% on sampled set -> rollback. Also tie into SLO burn rate.
[03:12] Samir: for security, we need the audit log retention confirmed and confirmation that no PII is stored in logs. also need SASL? (sic) — actually we use SAML/SSO, sorry.
[03:26] Maya: noted, we'll include audit log retention table in the pack.

--- Runbook and responsibilities ---
[03:34] Maya: runbook steps: pre-cutover checklist, small canary routing config (traffic switches), smoke tests, metrics validation, rollback, post-mortem notes. who owns smoke tests?
[03:44] Diego: SRE will own smoke scripts and will run them, but Redwood SE should provide the smoke test harness and expected output.
[03:51] Liam: I'll hand over a smoke harness (simple curl + checksum) and a script that validates KV cache warmup. we'll also provide expected token/latency baselines.
[04:05] Priya: who watches? Aurora wants on-call names and escalation path.
[04:09] Sofia (CSM): Redwood will be on standby for the canary window, I'll coordinate the escalation list.
[04:15] Maya: we also recommend a quiet-window approach: disable non-essential jobs, freeze deployments 1 hour before.
[04:23] Elena: agree. also request that we keep single-region routing for the canary initially to avoid cross-region variability.

--- Monitoring and alerting ---
[04:30] Liam: primary dashboards: token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latencies, model error rates, hallucination sampling metric. We'll push SLO alerts to Aurora's PagerDuty.
[04:44] Diego: can we get Prometheus metrics endpoint? the company standard is Prometheus + Grafana, plus PD.
[04:50] Liam: yes we can expose a Prom exporter. there may be label name mismatches, the SE will share a mapping document.
[04:58] Nora: on hallucination sampling, how frequent will samples be? we need enough to detect the 2% threshold with statistical power.
[05:06] Liam: initial config: sample 1% of traffic up to 1k samples per hour, run a lightweight entity-extraction validation. if variance high we'll increase sampling.

--- Risks and mitigation ---
[05:20] Priya: main risk is regression in production for critical entities. mitigation?
[05:25] Nora: we keep canary small and use an evaluation set of high-sensitivity prompts. also toggle to model variant A which is more conservative if issues occur.
[05:36] Maya: Redwood's automatic fallback policy can route to a smaller quantized model or to a cold fallback API endpoint (hosted) — it can add cost but buys availability.
[05:48] Diego: cost tradeoffs, yes we need a cost blowout guard — maybe an automatic budget cap that reduces throughput if cost exceeds threshold.
[05:56] Liam: we can set routing policy by cost band, but that needs configuring ahead of time.

--- Security and compliance ---
[06:05] Samir: SOC2 artifacts, encryption at rest details, KMS integration questions. will the platform support our HSM-backed keys?
[06:17] Maya: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations; for the hosted path we can use customer-managed keys in some regions. we'll send the exact fields.
[06:26] Samir: also need contract language for data residency in EU—some of our PHI flows live in EU.
[06:32] Elena: question - for the pilot are we operating under the hosted environment or dedicated?
[06:36] Maya: pilot is on Dedicated pool in us-west for now; for EU residency we can propose a private deployment or dedicated in EU region for go-live.

--- Final alignment and decisions ---
[06:45] Priya: decisions so far: canary next Tue 10% for 6hr, roll to 50% if gates pass, rollback criteria as stated; Redwood to deliver security pack and runbook template by Friday, cutover rehearsal week-of 24th.
[06:58] Elena: agree, and Aurora will confirm the PD routing and provide production-like traffic by Sunday.
[07:06] Maya: ok quick checklist of owners, we'll capture ASIs in action items. any outstanding questions?
[07:12] Samir: can you include encryption cipher details in the pack?
[07:16] Maya: yes we'll include ciphers and KMS options.
[07:20] Priya: can Redwood share a sample prometheus scrape config?
[07:23] Liam: yes, I'll attach a sample mapping.

Close:
[07:30] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in chat with links, recording and action items.
[07:36] Priya: thanks all.
[07:40] Elena: thanks.

Notes: transcription contains occasional misheard acronyms (SASL vs SAML) and dropped words; timestamps approximate. Links referenced: runbook-template (link sent post-call), security-pack (SOC2-summary.pdf).
questions: Can Redwood support HSM-backed KMS for hosted/dedicated?
What are exact rollback thresholds for latency, errors, hallucination rate?
Who will run and own smoke tests and alerts during canary?
